note: Real machine run. Medians of N after per-case warmup. Updating this file is a reviewed commit, never a reflex. 2026-09-14 (P2-F-1): schema v2 — every case now carries `class` (deterministic/wall-clock/browser); wall-clock cases additionally carry `ratio` (median normalised against this run's fixed calibration workload, not the machine-bound `median` itself, which stays for humans only) and a top-level `calibrationMs` records the calibration figure this baseline was minted against, for audit. `cold-load-recorded` is renamed `cold-load-transcribed` (its stale entry under the old id is removed) and marked `transcribed: true` so the runner's own table -- not just this file's comment -- shows it is copied from a Playwright run, never re-timed. `client-js-gzip` jumps 52.05kB -> 116.5kB (~97% of the 120kB budget): no code changed here: this is the first re-baseline since v0.2.0 to actually run after the whole of Phase 2 landed on this branch (library panel, stat engine, charts, Ruleset Studio, and the dedicated bench worker all shipped without anyone re-running `--update-baseline`), so five tasks' worth of client growth show up in one jump. Genuinely worth watching before Phase 3 adds more; not a P2-F-1 regression. `default-theme-palette-lookup`, `paint-1m`, `snapshot-restore`, `seek-4000` and `zobrist-update` no longer gate nothing (their pre-P2-F-1 state) -- they are `wall-clock` now and their `ratio` is a real gate. Every other case's `median` moved only by sandbox-to-sandbox noise (see the wall-clock class's noise-aware tolerance, §3.6) -- `snapshot-restore` and `seek-4000` swing tens of percent on this box because a sub-millisecond timer is dominated by scheduling jitter here, which is exactly the noise the ratio gate is designed to absorb, not eliminate. 2026-09-14 (P2-F-3 closeout): `zobrist-update` and `stats-overhead` are self-calibrated (already a same-process ratio / overhead %). Their committed `ratio` is now `1/median`, not `calibrationMs/median` — the previous formula made a faster calibrator look like a Zobrist regression (CI run 34892209486: 0.998 vs 1.004 cost ratio flagged +17.3% because calibration went 8.78ms → 7.22ms). `stats-overhead` median re-recorded from that same ubuntu-latest run (4.318%, still under the 5% budget) so the 12% band is against CI, not the sandbox. `seek-4000` keeps its P2-F-1 median (0.237 ms): a later GHA run of the mean-of-32 case landed at 0.0776 ms against a lucky 0.0387 ms floor and false-failed +30.5% while remaining ~3000× under the 250 ms budget.
